info.title: Spotlight Control Plane
info.description:
HTTP API for the Spotlight Control Plane.

## Resource conventions

Operations marked `x-spotlight-resource` manage configuration resources, the ones the Terraform provider writes. They live under `/v1/resources` and address everything by id. Every resource follows these rules, and a conformance suite checks each one against them.

- **Stable ids.** Spotlight issues a resource's `id` when it is created. It never changes for the resource's life, whatever else does.
- **Reads return every field.** A read returns the whole resource, defaults filled in, so a client comparing it with what it wrote sees any drift. A write returns exactly what a read returns.
- **Versions.** Every resource carries a `version` that rises with each change, and each response carries it as a strong `ETag` (`"3"`). An update or delete must send it back as `If-Match`: without one it fails with 428, and against a version that is no longer current with 409, whose body gives the `currentVersion` and whose `ETag` names it. A write that would remove something another resource still uses fails with 409 `in-use`.
- **Idempotent creates.** A create must carry an `Idempotency-Key`. Retrying with the same key and body within 24 hours returns the resource that the first attempt created, marked `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, and creates nothing more; the same key with a different body fails with 422.
- **Problems name fields.** Errors are `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457). `type` is stable and safe to branch on. An invalid request lists `errors`, each with the `path` of the attribute it is about, as in `stations[2].check`; a key that is not a plain name is quoted, as Terraform addresses it: `on["task.opened"].to.thread`.
- **API versions.** The path names the major version, as in `/v1`; a change that is not additive gets a new path. Within it, a client may send `Spotlight-Api-Version`; every response names the version that it uses, currently `2026-09-23`. Changes within a version are additive only: fields and operations are added, never removed, renamed or given a new meaning.
- **Expression checks.** `POST /v1/expressions/check` type-checks one CEL expression at the attribute that contains it, named within the resource's whole definition (`integration.webhook.events[0].when`), as `terraform plan` needs. What the expression may read is worked out from that definition exactly as applying it would, so a plan fails where an apply would; a definition that has an error fails with 422, each error under `definition`. It returns the type and any errors, each with the span it is about and a suggestion where a declared name is near, and warnings about the definition, such as a capture shadowing a built-in name. `GET /v1/expressions/positions` lists every position, with `[*]` for any index or key, and the variables an expression there can read. They follow these headers and problems, but are not resources.
- **Credentials.** A client calls with a person's session or with a workspace token. A script or Terraform sends a workspace token, or the login that `spotlight login` stores, as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A login acts as its person, with that person's role. A token acts only within its own workspace and only as its scopes allow. `read`, `plan` and `configure` are a ladder: `read` reads, `plan` also checks expressions, and `configure` also creates, updates and deletes configuration as a workspace admin may, except secrets, runners and OIDC trusts. `secrets` is granted beside one of them and lets the token create, rebind, rotate and delete secrets; Terraform that manages secrets uses `["configure", "secrets"]`. `runners` is granted the same way and lets the token create, rekey and delete runners and runner trusts and create, update and delete the workspace's runners, since a runner claims runs, checks out repositories and keeps git credentials; Terraform that manages runners uses `["configure", "runners"]`. `trusts` is granted the same way and lets the token create, update and delete OIDC trusts, since a trust hands out tokens; a token can only create a trust that grants scopes it has itself, so bootstrap the trusts once with a token that has `trusts` and every scope they grant, as in `["configure", "secrets", "trusts"]`, and revoke it. No token manages members or tokens, or reads the audit.
- **CI without a stored token.** A workspace admin, or a token granted `trusts`, creates an OIDC trust naming an OIDC issuer, audience, subject and claims, and the scopes and lifetime (at most an hour) of the tokens it issues. A CI job exchanges the OIDC token its platform issues it at `POST /v1/workspace-tokens/exchange` with `{ "trust": <trust id>, "token": <OIDC token> }`, and calls with the short-lived token it gets back. Deleting the trust stops every token that it issued at once, and the audit names the trust and the workload's subject beside each exchange and each change made with an issued token.
- **Forbidden changes.** A change by someone who may read the resource but not change it, person or token, fails with 403 `forbidden`, whose `permission` names what the caller lacks, one of `configure`, `secrets`, `runners`, `trusts`, `administer`, `create-workspaces`, `plan`. Anything they may not see at all returns 404.
- **Who changed what.** A client names itself in `Spotlight-Client` (`terraform-provider/<version>` or `web`), and every configuration change is recorded with who made it, person or token, and through which client. A secret's change also records the value version it moved to and the hosts it is bound to, never its value.
- **Import by address.** Each resource has an `address` that names it within its workspace, such as `core/linear`, and an import operation that returns the resource at that address, as `terraform import` needs. A workspace's address is its slug; a team's is its key; anything a team owns is the team's key and its own, as in `core/delivery`.

runnerId.description: The one-run runner Spotlight started for this work. Null for a sandbox with no run.

token.description: The one-run credential, good only for this work and only until it ends; every later call carries it instead of the host’s own credential. Null for a sandbox with no run.

egressToken.description: The credential the egress sidecar fetches the run’s secrets with; the host hands it to egress alone, never into the sandbox. Null for a sandbox with no run: its egress starts with no secrets.

sandboxId.description: The sandbox Spotlight started for a run; the host labels its container with it and reports it in each heartbeat. Null for a check.

sandboxToken.description: The credential of a new sandbox, for its own calls only: restore and archive its workspace. The host hands it into the sandbox with the first assignment. Null when the run reuses a live sandbox, and for a check.

allowedHosts.description: Hosts the egress of a sandbox with no run lets through: where the sandbox restores and stores its workspace archives. Empty for a run: its egress reads them with the run’s secrets.

reused.description: The run goes into the live sandbox the claim named, not into a new one. The host delivers its assignment into that container.

host.description: The host claiming, as it names itself in its heartbeat

id.description: The call, to answer by once it has been sent

url.description: Where to send it, from inside the host’s network

headers.description: Sent with the body, exactly as given

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for an answer, in milliseconds

host.description: The host that records the response, the one that claimed the call

status.description: The HTTP status of the response, or 0 when no response came

body.description: The body of the response, base64, at most 16 KiB

ms.description: How long the call took to get a response, in milliseconds

error.description: Why no response came, when the status is 0

recipient.description: The X25519 public key that egress holds for this run alone, in base64; values Spotlight stores are sealed to it

proxyCredential.description: The run proxy credential a runner presented to a shared egress. A shared egress sends it with its own egress token; an egress sidecar leaves it out

host.description: The one host that egress injects it for

location.description: Whether egress injects it in a request header or in a query parameter

name.description: The header or query parameter that contains its stand-in

sealed.description: The value, sealed to the recipient for this run; null when egress reads it in its own network

externalRef.description: Where egress reads the value with its host’s own identity; null when Spotlight sealed it

reason.example: The workspace has no secret named LINEAR_API_KEY; create it before anything uses it

sealed.description: A read and plan token for this run alone, sealed to the recipient; egress injects it for the control plane as a bearer token

runId.description: The run the sealed values are bound to; null when the sandbox checks a change stack and gets no secrets

extraAllowedHosts.description: Hosts that every sandbox is allowed to connect to besides the control plane, whatever else the host allows

bound.description: The hosts the secrets are bound to. Egress decrypts only these hosts, and also the control plane host when spotlightApi is set

denied.description: The secrets of the run that egress does not get, and why

spotlightApi.description: Where the run uses Spotlight’s own API, the token that it uses

proxyCredential.description: The run proxy credential a runner presented to the egress

controlPlaneHost.description: The host of the control plane URL the runner was handed. Before the runner has a run, egress allows it to connect only to this host

controlPlanePort.description: The port of the control plane URL the runner was handed. Egress allows a sandbox to connect to the control plane host only on this port

extraAllowedHosts.description: Hosts that every sandbox is allowed to connect to besides the control plane, whatever else the egress allows

proxyCredentials.description: The run proxy credentials whose runs the egress serves now

active.description: The proxy credentials whose runner still leases its work, or has no work yet. Egress evicts the secrets of every other run

bytesOut.description: Bytes from the sandbox to the host

bytesIn.description: Bytes from the host to the sandbox

ms.description: How long the connection was open

status.description: The status the host answered an injected request with. Egress cannot read the status of a passthrough connection

reason.description: Why egress blocked the connection or could not open it. Spotlight drops a record whose reason does not fit its outcome

bootId.description: New each time the host starts, so a restart shows as one

name.description: What the host calls itself, usually its hostname

containerRuntime.description: The container runtime its sandboxes run in

capacity.description: How many sandboxes it runs at once

running.description: The one-run runners in its sandboxes now

sandboxes.description: The sandboxes whose containers it has now

images.description: The runner images it supports or cannot use, each with what it found inside

stopping.description: True when the host stopped claiming to update or restart. Spotlight then drains each of its sandboxes when no run holds it

workspace.description: The workspace the host serves, which it keeps its mirrors under

drain.description: The reported sandboxes to drain: the host stops each one with a grace period, then destroys it

harnesses.description: The harnesses the runner found installed, each with the models it discovered. What is on a machine is a fact about that machine, so the machine is what says it.

diff.description: The changes, as the output of git diff

repository.description: Which checkout the changes are from

base.description: The commit of the checkout when the run began

code.description: Why the runner could not check the stack at all

detail.description: What it printed while trying, where that helps

step.description: The step it ran: "whole", or the layer it checked

output.description: The end of what the check printed

skipped.description: Set where the stack could not be checked at all

index.description: The position of the step in its run

kind.description: message, thought, planned, handover, or remember

text.example: A queue would need a worker we do not run.

position.description: The position of the note on its task

by.description: person: a teammate signed in to Spotlight; world: someone writing through another tool

author.description: The teammate who wrote it; absent for a note from another tool, which carries no author

text.example: Never retry an upload rejected with a 403.

body.example: Never retry an upload the bucket rejected with a 403.

source.description: person: only notes by a teammate; outside: input the team does not control, approved one at a time; run: anything else

proposedBy.description: drafter: the drafter read it from the run after the run ended; agent: the agent proposed it with spotlight remember

scope.description: Where it applies: the whole team, its line, or its station

supersedes.description: The active memory it replaces after approval

decision.description: Who approved or rejected it, and when

harness.description: The harness of the run whose steps it cites

steps.description: The steps of its run that it cites

notes.description: The notes on the task that it cites

by.description: Who retired it; nobody where a newer memory superseded it

handle.description: How runs and people name it, as in spotlight recall M-12

provenance.description: The task and run it cites; none where a person wrote it

runs.description: How many runs were briefed with it or recalled it

handle.description: How runs and people name it, as in spotlight recall M-12

provenance.description: The task and run it cites; none where a person wrote it

runs.description: How many runs were briefed with it or recalled it

harness.description: The harness of the run whose steps it cites

body.example: Uploads retry in the request, not from a queue.

scope.description: Where it applies; the run’s line when left out

paths.description: Paths it is about, relative to the run’s workspace, each starting with the checkout folder

supersedes.description: The active memory it corrects, by handle

path.description: Where to write it, relative to the run’s workspace

body.example:
# M-18 · rationale

Uploads retry in the request.

name.description: A slug unique in the search: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter or digit, at most 63 characters

hypothesis.example: A shorter prompt keeps it on the failing test.
hypothesis.description: What the candidate is expected to improve, and why

station.description: The station block, as the line stores it, changed only where a search may change it

replayId.description: Its replay on the search’s searched tasks, started now

taskId.description: A failing task the reflection’s briefing lists, by its task id

cause.description: config when a change to the station’s config could fix it; task when the task itself is why; judge when the judge scored it wrong; check when the check failed for a reason the change did not cause; infra when the run failed around the work

evidence.description: What in the runs shows the cause, in 1 to 4000 characters

suggestion.description: What a person, or the next iteration, should change, in at most 4000 characters

replayRunId.description: The failing replay run the cause is about
